title: Page State Envelope
description:
The serializable state of one rendered page: which parameters, filters, selections and active tabs produced the view on screen.

The runtime already holds this state; what it has never had is a NAME for it, and four capabilities all need one:

1. **Deep links.** `syncToUrl` is declared throughout the page model and a URL is just this envelope, serialized. Without a defined envelope every surface invents its own encoding and links stop round-tripping.
2. **Support and reproduction.** A defect in a governed platform is reproducible from definition version, identity and state. Two of those three were already addressable; this is the third.
3. **Agent context.** An agent must be told what the user is looking at. Handing it this envelope is bounded, reviewable and free of data; handing it the rendered page is none of those things.
4. **Restore.** Returning to a workspace where you left it is a state restore, not a navigation.

What this envelope must NEVER carry is as important as what it carries. No data rows: state is what was asked, not what came back. No entitlement decision: those are resolved from identity at request time and a cached decision travelling in a link is an authorization bypass. No transient runtime state — an in-flight write, an optimistic value, an unsent agent proposal — because that state is not something a user should be able to restore into, and a link that resurrects a half-finished write is a defect with a governance consequence.

definitionVersion.description: The artifact version this state was captured against. State is only meaningful relative to a definition: a filter channel that no longer exists must be dropped on restore rather than silently retained, and that requires knowing which version produced it.

params.description: Declared page and experience parameters, by id. Values are literals — a parameter whose default is an expression is resolved before capture, because a restored link must mean the same thing tomorrow as it does today.

filters.description: Filter channel values. Null and empty are meaningfully different from absent: absent means the channel was never set, null means it was explicitly cleared, and a restore must reproduce the distinction or a cleared filter comes back set.

selections.description: Selection channel contents, as the key fields the channel declares — never a row index, which would not survive a re-query, and never a whole row, which would put data in the envelope.

activeTabs.description: Active tab per tabs container, keyed by layout node id. Present because a tab is page state that a user expects a link to preserve — and for a data-driven tabs container the tab id is a row identity, which is why it must be captured as a value rather than as an index.

paging.description: Per-data-source paging position. Optional, and deliberately not part of a shareable link by default: a colleague opening a link expects the top of the queue, not page seven of a result set that has since changed.

capturedBy.description: Who captured it, for a support bundle. Never used to resolve authorization on restore — the restoring caller's own identity decides what they see, which is why the same link legitimately renders differently for two people.

purpose.description: Why the envelope exists. 'link' and 'restore' round-trip through the URL and session; 'support' may be attached to a defect report; 'agentContext' is the projection handed to an agent turn. The distinction matters because a support bundle may legitimately carry more than a shareable link should.

stateValue.description: A literal or a list of literals. Deliberately not a computable value: state is the RESOLVED result of one, and storing the wrapper instead would make a link's meaning depend on when it was opened.
